title: Past continuous (I was doing)
subtitle: I was doing
summary: Use the past continuous (was/were + -ing) for an action you were in the middle of at a time in the past, and combine it with the past simple for things that happened in the middle of it.

lesson.heading: Study this situation
lesson.text: Yesterday Karen and Joe played tennis. They started at 10 o'clock and finished at 11.30. So, at 10.30 **they were playing** tennis. they were playing = they were in the middle of playing, they had not finished. **was/were + -ing** is the past continuous.

examples.note: = in the middle of playing; not finished

lesson.heading: In the middle of doing something
lesson.text: **I was doing** something = I was in the middle of doing it at a certain time. The action or situation started before this time, but had not finished.

examples.text: This time last year **I was living** in Hong Kong.
What **were you doing** at 10 o'clock last night?
I waved to Helen, but she **wasn't looking**.

lesson.heading: I was doing and I did

left.label: I was doing (past continuous)
left.text: = in the middle of an action
examples: We **were walking** home when I met Dan. (in the middle of walking home)
Kate **was watching** TV when we arrived.

right.label: I did (past simple)
examples: We **walked** home after the party last night. (= all the way, completely)
Kate **watched** TV a lot when she was ill last year.

lesson.heading: Something happened in the middle of something else
lesson.text: You can say that something happened (past simple) in the middle of something else (past continuous). But we use the past simple to say that one thing happened *after* another.

examples.text: I saw you in the park yesterday. You **were sitting** on the grass and reading a book.
I **hurt** my back while I **was working** in the garden.
I was walking along the road when I **saw** Dan. So I **stopped**, and we **talked** for a while.
examples.note: one thing after another: past simple

left.label: we were having dinner
left.text: = we had already started before she arrived
examples: When Karen arrived, we **were having** dinner.

right.label: we had dinner
right.text: = Karen arrived, and then we had dinner

lesson.heading: Verbs not used in continuous forms
lesson.text: Some verbs (for example **know** and **want**) are not normally used in continuous forms (is + -ing, was + -ing etc.). Use the past simple for them.

examples.text: We were good friends. We **knew** each other well.
I was enjoying the party, but Chris **wanted** to go home.

lesson.text: Background action (longer, already in progress) = was/were + -ing. The event that interrupts it (shorter, sudden) = past simple: I was cycling home when a man stepped out.

exercises.prompt: 'What did he say?' 'I don't know. I ___.'
exercises.explanation: In the middle of not listening at that moment in the past: I wasn't listening.

exercises.prompt: We ___ at the back of the theatre. We couldn't hear very well.
exercises.explanation: A situation in progress in the past: we were sitting.

exercises.prompt: Which goes with which? Match the two halves of each sentence.

pairs.left: When I got to the cafe
pairs.right: my friends were waiting for me.
while we were watching a film.
when she was living in Rome.

pairs.left: Tom didn't come out with us
The car began to make a strange noise

exercises.prompt: I saw you in your car. Where ___?
exercises.explanation: Question in the past continuous: were + subject + -ing.

exercises.prompt: Ask your friend what they were doing at 10 o'clock last night.
exercises.answer: What were you doing at 10 o'clock last night?
exercises.explanation: A certain time in the past + an action in progress: What were you doing?

exercises.prompt: '___ out last night?' 'No, I was too tired.'
exercises.explanation: A complete action (or not) in the past: past simple with did.

exercises.prompt: Sam ___ a picture of me while I wasn't looking.
exercises.explanation: Taking the picture is the short, complete action in the middle of the longer one (I wasn't looking): took.

exercises.prompt: I ___ home yesterday when a man stepped out into the road in front of me.
exercises.explanation: The longer background action is past continuous: I was cycling; the man stepped out (past simple) in the middle of it.

exercises.statement: I hurt my back while I was working in the garden.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Something happened (hurt) in the middle of something else (was working).

exercises.prompt: When Karen arrived, we ___ dinner - we had already started before she came.
exercises.explanation: Already in progress when she arrived: we were having dinner. 'We had dinner' would mean we started after she arrived.

exercises.statement: We were good friends. We were knowing each other well.
exercises.explanation: We knew each other well. know is not normally used in continuous forms.

exercises.prompt: Last night I dropped a plate when I ___ the washing up. Fortunately it didn't break.
exercises.explanation: Doing the washing up was in progress when the plate dropped: I was doing.
